near: Edit this image. It is an unfinished top-down satellite view, looking straight down, of a small cyclone in the cloud tops of Jupiter, lit by a low sun from the upper left. The fan-shaped part in the middle is partly finished: just below the center lies the cyclone, a red-brown funnel with terraced spiral walls, with crisp cumulus towers around it; this sharp part is finished. Farther up inside the fan the clouds dissolve into soft radial smears, and everything outside the fan is only flat, smooth, blurred tan color with no detail: all of that is unfinished. Paint all unfinished and soft parts as the same cloud deck seen from straight above, to the same crisp finish as the sharp towers at the cyclone: a closed ring of tall puffy cumulus towers and cauliflower cloud tops all the way round the funnel, also below it and beside it where the picture is still flat, then lower cloud tops, folded turbulent filaments and small eddies farther out, each top lit from the upper left with a soft shadow falling to its lower right. Replace the radial smears by round cloud tops seen from above. The straight edges of the fan must disappear completely into continuous cloud. The dark blue-grey area at the right stays a dark blue-grey shadowed part of the deck, with the same kind of cloud tops in dim light, and fades out gradually. Keep the cyclone and its funnel exactly as they are, at the same size and place: do not enlarge it, do not add a second storm. Keep the colors and the brightness of every area as they are. Seen from straight above everywhere: no horizon, no perspective, no sky, no stars, no haze, no fog, no vignette, no text, no border. Square 1:1 image.
